basis: Anterior horn cell degeneration defines disease; weakness and amyotrophy reflect denervation. Structural foot damage at a frequency of at least 30% is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: denervation weakness and wasting do not establish direct muscle disease; frequency of damaging skeletal deformities is unspecified.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines disease; visual impairment occurs in 6/15 (40%). Joint hypermobility in 7/13 lacks documented joint injury or functional loss.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hypermobility in 7/13 establishes laxity, but does not by itself establish joint damage or loss of function.

basis: Long QT, syndactyly and neurodevelopmental abnormalities define disease; hypoglycemia 7/17 and hypocalcemia 6/17 support metabolic involvement. Microdontia 17/17 omitted at cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: microdontia occurs in 17/17, but dental involvement is less severe than the retained cardiac, neurologic, limb and metabolic abnormalities; omitted at cap.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hypoglycemia in 7/17 (41%) and hypocalcemia in 6/17 (35%) establish common metabolic dysfunction.

basis: LAM directly infiltrates and destroys pulmonary tissue. Renal angiomyolipomas and TSC-associated skin lesions are distinct associated diseases.

decisions.renal: none: renal angiomyolipoma is a separately diagnosed associated neoplasm, rather than renal damage directly caused by pulmonary LAM.

basis: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy defines disease. Small pituitary in 4/5 imaged patients does not establish endocrine dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: small pituitary in 4/5 is an anatomical finding without documented hormone deficiency or other endocrine loss of function.

basis: Localized lymphoid-cell proliferation defines unicentric Castleman disease; it is not inherently lymphoma, infection, immunodeficiency or an immune-mediated disease.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: localized Castleman disease is a lymphoproliferative disorder; immune-cell proliferation alone does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.

basis: Polyamine metabolic disorder with neurodevelopmental abnormalities and alopecia; ptosis affects 2/4 (50%). Hearing loss in one assessed patient does not establish prevalence.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis is eyelid dysfunction reported in 2/4 (50%), corroborated by a frequent bilateral-ptosis annotation.
decisions.otologic: none: sensorineural hearing impairment in one assessed patient is insufficient to establish occurrence in at least 30% of the syndrome population.

basis: Inherited amyloid protein-metabolism disorder prominently damages kidneys; symptomatic gastrointestinal deposition affects roughly one-third or more. Hepatic deposits may spare function.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hereditary lysozyme amyloidosis is a disorder of protein metabolism with pathological amyloid accumulation.

basis: Defining arthrogryposis, renal tubular dysfunction and cholestasis; platelet granule/aggregation defects affect 30-79%. Skin, CNS and gastrointestinal involvement omitted at cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: intrinsic platelet alpha-granule and aggregation defects occur in 30-79% and cause clinically important bleeding dysfunction.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: ARC is a vesicular-trafficking disorder; the bilirubin-metabolism ancestor does not establish a primary metabolic defect beyond cholestatic liver dysfunction.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: arthrogryposis is a defining component of the syndrome and occurs in 80-99%; congenital hip dislocation is also frequent.

basis: Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with structural skeletal involvement: rocker-bottom feet in 3/3 and hip dislocation in 2/3. No established systemic metabolic phenotype.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: AARS-related encephalopathy concerns tRNA aminoacylation; the amino-acid-transport ancestor does not establish a metabolic disorder in this concept.
